subsystems.name: Alternative backbone
subsystems.role: replaces the natural deoxyribose/ribose sugar with a different chemistry that can still carry sequence information.
parts: non-natural sugars (threose, hexitol, glycerol, cyclohexenyl, arabino, 2′-fluoroarabino)

subsystems.name: Base pairs
subsystems.role: the letters written on that backbone — either the natural four bases or an expanded alphabet.
parts: unnatural base pairs with hydrophobic or alternative hydrogen-bonding patterns

subsystems.name: Engineered polymerases
subsystems.role: enzymes, obtained by directed evolution, that can copy DNA into XNA and XNA back into DNA.

subsystems.name: XNA catalysts (XNAzymes)
subsystems.role: XNA strands folded into shapes that catalyse reactions, including cutting and joining nucleic acids.

subsystems.name: Reading and quality control
subsystems.role: converts XNA back into DNA so it can be sequenced, and measures error rates.

subsystems.name: Host and containment
subsystems.role: a cell or acellular system that runs XNA chemistry without exchanging it with natural biology — the 'firewall'.

buildSteps.title: Choose a backbone chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Pick a sugar or linkage that still forms a stable, sequence-specific duplex with itself or with DNA/RNA.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the building blocks
buildSteps.detail: Chemically make the nucleoside triphosphates of that chemistry — the raw letters the enzymes will use.

buildSteps.title: Evolve a polymerase
buildSteps.detail: Start from a thermostable polymerase, build large mutant libraries, and repeatedly select variants that accept the unnatural triphosphates and copy a template without stalling.

buildSteps.title: Store information
buildSteps.detail: Run PCR-like cycles in XNA: copy DNA into XNA, then XNA back into DNA, checking that the sequence survives intact.

buildSteps.title: Evolve catalytic XNA
buildSteps.detail: Select pools of random XNA sequences for function, yielding XNAzymes that cleave or ligate nucleic acids — proof the polymer is not just inert storage.

buildSteps.title: Move into a cell
buildSteps.detail: Engineer a host to take up the unnatural precursors and replicate XNA inside it, then show the XNA is inherited over generations.

buildSteps.title: Read and correct
buildSteps.detail: Reverse-transcribe and sequence the products to quantify fidelity; add proofreading or repair where errors are too high.

buildSteps.title: Build the firewall
buildSteps.detail: Make the system dependent on a nutrient natural organisms cannot use and give it no route to exchange genes with wild biology.

prerequisites.why: without custom monomers there is nothing for the enzymes to polymerise.
natural enzymes largely reject non-natural backbones; evolving acceptance is the central trick.
XNA fidelity can only be measured by copying back to DNA and reading it.
eight-letter DNA and bacteria carrying an unnatural base pair have been demonstrated, but not stable, scalable orthogonal genomes.
cells need transporters and kinases for unnatural nucleotides, and must not degrade or reject them.
a true firewall needs engineered dependencies whose failure modes are understood before any release.

pathway.milestone: XNA replication and XNAzyme catalysis demonstrated in vitro, plus expanded-alphabet systems in engineered microbes
pathway.unlocks: proof that heredity and catalysis are not exclusive to DNA and RNA.

pathway.milestone: XNA aptamers and XNAzymes used as medicines and diagnostics
pathway.unlocks: commercial value from the biostability of unnatural backbones, funding the harder work.

pathway.milestone: Self-sustaining orthogonal organisms that copy and select their own XNA
pathway.unlocks: a genuinely separate genetic system that can be engineered without touching natural genomes.

pathway.milestone: XNA-based biosynthesis and data storage inside contained hosts
pathway.unlocks: organisms or reactors making molecules and storing information that natural biology cannot.
